meta.notes: X posts used only as discovery leads and are not numbered sources. Videos listed in the companion markdown were not frame-reviewed by this seat.

sources.title: MDA: A Formal Approach to Game Design and Game Research
sources.author: Robin Hunicke, Marc LeBlanc, Robert Zubek
sources.observedEvidence: Full 5-page PDF inspected this session. Workshop origin GDC Game Design and Tuning 2001-2004. Defines mechanics/dynamics/aesthetics, eight aesthetic types, designer-vs-player reverse chain, Monopoly and babysitter tuning examples. AAAI Challenges in Game AI workshop, 2004.
sources.applicability: Shared vocabulary for locking intended feelings before features; tuning loop across three layers; any genre.
sources.limitations: Not a formula for fun. Aesthetic list is a compass. 2004 paper; later critiques of MDA exist and were not fully surveyed. Does not specify production scheduling.

sources.title: Game Design Workshop, 5th Edition — playcentric excerpt
sources.author: Tracy Fullerton
sources.observedEvidence: Author-posted excerpt dated 2024-04-18 for the 5th edition (CRC/Taylor & Francis, listed publication 2024-04-19). Defines player experience goals as felt situations, immediate physical prototyping, iteration against those goals, and the cost of late core-mechanic testing.
sources.applicability: Step 1 overlay and every later playtest gate. Works for digital and analog. Strong for solo and teaching.
sources.limitations: Full 5th edition not read cover-to-cover. Physical prototypes under-serve real-time feel (see S06). Friend playtests bias results (see Fulton comments adjacent to S08).

sources.title: The Art of Game Design: A Book of Lenses (studio hub)
sources.author: Jesse Schell
sources.observedEvidence: Official Schell Games page fetched 2026-09-22. Describes 100+ lenses as question-sets, Deck of Lenses, companion app. First edition August 2008 (Elsevier); third edition CRC 2019 with VR/AR and modern examples per publisher listings.
sources.applicability: Diagnostic questions when a prototype feels wrong; shared team language; platform-agnostic including board games and attractions.
sources.limitations: Book text not read cover-to-cover. Deck/app are untested tools. Using all 100 lenses as a checklist is a misuse the method itself warns against.

sources.title: GDC 2012: Sid Meier on interesting decisions
sources.author: Sid Meier (Firaxis); write-up Leigh Alexander
sources.observedEvidence: Contemporary Gamasutra/Game Developer write-up 2012-03-07 inspected. Covers always-A and random-choice failure tests, tradeoffs, situational choices, play-style expression, information, feedback, player types, cutting ~1/3 of tried systems. Official GDC YouTube upload 2018-09-27 listed for parent frame review; not watched end-to-end here.
sources.applicability: Any game whose play is choices under uncertainty. Useful during ideation and ruthless cutting in Step 10.
sources.limitations: Meier states rhythm and some puzzle games are a weaker fit. Civilization-heavy examples. Video not frame-reviewed by this seat.

sources.title: A Theory of Fun for Game Design — author page and 2003 slides
sources.author: Raph Koster
sources.observedEvidence: Author page fetched. 2003 Austin Game Conference keynote slides hosted by the author; book 2004 (Paraglyph), 2nd edition 2013 (O'Reilly). Thesis: fun is the brain rewarding pattern learning; games bore once the pattern is mastered; long-lived games refresh possibility space.
sources.applicability: Skill games, combat-as-puzzle, mastery curves, why live permutation appears.
sources.limitations: Author himself notes the talk is not full ludology. Weak on fellowship/atmosphere/submission-as-pastime aesthetics from S01. Full book not read cover-to-cover.

sources.title: Game Feel: A Game Designer's Guide to Virtual Sensation
sources.author: Steve Swink
sources.observedEvidence: Publisher pages and Library of Congress TOC inspected. First published 2008-10-13, Morgan Kaufmann/CRC. TOC names defining feel, perception, interactivity model, metrics for input/response/context/metaphor. Associated playset website historically claimed; not exercised.
sources.applicability: Real-time control of a virtual object; input latency, spatial simulation, polish. Feel-track prototypes.
sources.limitations: Book not read cover-to-cover. Does not apply cleanly to turn-based or non-spatial games. Playset tool untested. 2008 vintage for input hardware examples.

sources.title: The Door Problem
sources.author: Liz England
sources.observedEvidence: 2014-04-21 essay. Live site fetch returned a stub; Wayback 2023-10-23 and Kotaku reprint 2016-05-03 (author permission stated) corroborate the question list and role-mapped 'other door problems'. 2025 Game Developer podcast exists for later leadership framing; not frame-reviewed.
sources.applicability: Spec template for every interactable; teaching what a designer does; hidden-scope discovery.
sources.limitations: Live URL unstable in this session. Essay is analogy, not a complete GDD standard. Large-studio role map does not transfer 1:1 to solo.

sources.title: Conversations From GDC Europe: Harvey Smith on systemic level design
sources.author: Harvey Smith (Ion Storm); interview John McLean-Foreman
sources.observedEvidence: Interview dated 2002-09-11 inspected. Defines systemic vs special-case levels, class-to-class interactions, second-order consequences, exploding-enemy-plus-container example, reward-for-goal-not-method. Same article includes Bill Fulton on usability methods.
sources.applicability: Immersive sims and any game that wants improvisation. Architecture ADR: systems vs set pieces.
sources.limitations: Deus Ex-era examples. Original GDC slides/audio not recovered first-party this session. Systemic design has production and QA cost not quantified here.

sources.title: Would the Real Emergent Gameplay Please Stand Up? (GDC 2004)
sources.author: Harvey Smith and Randy Smith
sources.observedEvidence: GDC Vault listing and unofficial 2017-10-20 YouTube reconstruction (slides + original audio). Transcript snippets: emergence from connected mechanics; general stimuli rather than object-pair hardcoding. Not frame-reviewed.
sources.applicability: How to increase possibility space without scripting every combo. Complements S08.
sources.limitations: No first-party video inspected. Unofficial reconstruction may omit slides. Randy Smith's separate 'object-oriented level design' essay was not found as a stable canonical URL.

sources.title: An Approach to Holistic Level Design (GDC 2017)
sources.author: Steve Lee (then Arkane Studios)
sources.observedEvidence: GDC YouTube 2017-07-18, ~49:38. Description and transcript snippets: holistic = gameplay + presentation + story as one; immersive-sim informed (Dishonored 2, BioShock); architecture-school parallel. Distinct from The Level Design Book (S11).
sources.applicability: 3D action-adventure and immersive-sim spaces; teaching level designers to own more than encounter blocking.
sources.limitations: Talk not frame-reviewed. Lee flags genre bias. Not a general 2D/puzzle/management-game process.

sources.title: The Level Design Book — How to make a level
sources.author: Robert Yang (founder); Andrew Yoder and volunteer contributors
sources.observedEvidence: Process page fetched. Eight-phase menu (pre-production, optional combat, layout, blockout, scripting, lighting, env art, release). Tailor-the-process warnings. License CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Self-labeled heavily under construction. Recent updates January 2025 (recommended talks) and November 2025 (Trenchbroom/tools cleanup). Disclaimer: usually FPS/TPS action.
sources.applicability: Spatial games. Blockout-before-art freeze. Group vs solo planning weight.
sources.limitations: Incomplete pages possible. Shooter-weighted. Not authored by Steve Lee (common conflation). Volunteer living doc; structure may change.

sources.title: A Game Design Vocabulary: Exploring the Foundational Principles Behind Good Game Design
sources.author: Anna Anthropy and Naomi Clark
sources.observedEvidence: Publisher listings (Addison-Wesley, 2014-02/03, ISBN 978-0-321-88692-7). Sample pages: verbs/objects/scenes; Anthropy part I, Clark part II. Liz England 2015-04-20 review describes it as short, practical, immediately usable.
sources.applicability: Naming the core verb; scene-level craft; teaching; small authored games; alternative to genre-first ideation.
sources.limitations: Full book not read. Less operational for large live economies. England notes it was relatively unknown even in 2015.

sources.title: Game Design: Theory & Practice (2nd edition) — author site
sources.author: Richard Rouse III
sources.observedEvidence: Author site fetched. 1st ed. 2001-02, 2nd ed. 2004-09 (Wordware). Covers brainstorming through playtesting; interviews (Meier, Wright, Mechner, Church, others); full Suffering design document in 2nd ed.
sources.applicability: What a complete GDD can contain; historical process coverage; documentation after a focus is chosen.
sources.limitations: 2004 platform/live-ops chapters are historical. Risk of document-first culture if used before paper prototypes (conflicts with S02). Full book not read.

sources.title: The Gamer's Brain — GDC talks and book record
sources.author: Celia Hodent
sources.observedEvidence: GDC 2015 talk on GDC YouTube (upload 2017-08-13) metadata and transcript snippets: intended vs actual experience, perception/attention/memory, UX guidelines, Wason-card demo. Parts 2 and 3 exist. Book 2017; 2nd edition CRC listed eBook 2026-03-05. GDC speaker bio lists Ubisoft, LucasArts, Epic/Fortnite UX.
sources.applicability: Readable UI, onboarding, cognitive load, hypothesis-driven playtests. Steps 3, 6, 7.
sources.limitations: Talks not frame-reviewed. Full books not read. Neuroscience popularization can be over-claimed if used as authority rather than testable guidelines. Fortnite-scale UX org does not transfer to solo.

sources.title: Xbox Accessibility Guidelines V3.2
sources.author: Microsoft Xbox / Gaming Accessibility (ms.author edigonzales on Learn page)
sources.observedEvidence: Official Learn page fetched. v3.2 published 2023-06-08. Page ms.date 2026-08-14, updated_at 2026-08-18. Explicitly not a legal compliance checklist. Per-XAG structure: goal, overview, scoping questions, implementation, examples, player impact, resources. Guidelines 101–123 listed.
sources.applicability: Scoping at ideation; implementation guidelines for input, time, contrast, audio buses, motion, documentation. Any platform can use the questions.
sources.limitations: Xbox-example-heavy. Not law. MGATS testing service not used here. Completeness of every XAG body was sampled, not every guideline page fully read.

sources.title: Steam Playtest (Steamworks Documentation)
sources.author: Valve (Steamworks)
sources.observedEvidence: Partner docs fetched 2026-09-22. Child AppID, store-page signup, Limited vs Open, random grants, country filter, deactivate Not Playable, no unique store page, cannot charge, not NDA, friend invites experimental, reset procedure, confidential-unannounced warning, demo/early-access distinction. Steam Direct $100 fee documented on related pages.
sources.applicability: Public scale playtests after a coming-soon page; official alternative to fake demos. Step 9/14 overlay.
sources.limitations: Untested in this research (no partner account used). PC-storefront-specific. Not a lab. Leak risk if misused for unannounced games. Valve's wishlist-noninterference claim not independently measured.

sources.title: Accessibility Features (Steamworks Documentation)
sources.author: Valve (Steamworks)
sources.observedEvidence: Docs fetched 2026-09-22. Store widget, search filters, Accessibility Feature Wizard. Tags for difficulty, save-anytime, volume buses, narration, subtitles, color, contrast, camera comfort, input-only modes, no-QTE, own-pace, chat TTS/STT. Explicit warning not to tag 'playable without vision' if only menus are narrated.
sources.applicability: Honest store communication after features exist. Complements S15 as player-facing labels, not as the design method.
sources.limitations: Tags are not a design process. Wizard answers can be gamed. ESA Accessible Games Initiative (2025) may change tag landscape; mapping incomplete.

sources.title: Xbox-GDK-Samples (including AccessibilitySample)
sources.author: Microsoft Xbox Advanced Technology Group
sources.observedEvidence: README and LICENSE fetched. MIT License, Copyright Microsoft. Public repo. Samples require October 2025 GDK; old layout deprecated. AccessibilitySample described as cross-platform accessibility demonstration. Commit history present (52 commits reported on main). Stars not used as quality.
sources.applicability: Reference implementation if shipping on GDK/Xbox/PC Game Pass. Proof that Microsoft publishes maintained accessibility sample code.
sources.limitations: GDK-oriented; many creators will never compile it. Sample telemetry block sends executable name to Microsoft unless removed. Not a design method. Unity samples still on old layout per README.
